documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I need refills on the Advair-type one and the Spiriva capsules. Pharmacy says no refills left. Also new year so I guess my insurance card changed, same plans though. Thanks, Steve

documents.title: Re: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Both inhalers renewed for 90 days with refills through the spring. Please bring the new cards to your next visit or upload a photo in the portal. Your next COPD check should be in May; the front desk will reach out.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring check on his lungs. Got through another winter without a flare needing steroids. Breathing is about where it has been for the last year: one flight, then a rest. Coughs on waking and in the evenings, sometimes hard enough to bring tears. Albuterol 3 to 5 times a week.

Inhalers: tiotropium mornings, fluticasone/salmeterol twice a day, rinsing after. Technique reviewed with the HandiHaler and Diskus; both fine.

Tobacco: still a pack and a half a day. Asked about smoking; he knows where we stand and said he is not going to make promises.

Pulmonology: due for his next visit there; he has not heard from them about scheduling and will call.

Exam: alert, talking comfortably. Lungs: diminished breath sounds throughout, prolonged expiration, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular rate and rhythm. No edema. No clubbing.

Assessment and plan:
1. COPD, GOLD Group C, with occupational bronchiolitis obliterans. Stable, no exacerbations in more than a year on triple inhaled therapy. No changes.
2. Tobacco dependence, 45 pack-years. Counseled.
3. Health maintenance: wellness visit due in June, labs then. Turns 50 in November; we will talk about the screening CT and shingles shots then.

Refills sent. Call or text with any change in breathing.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called to schedule his annual wellness visit. Pt said he would check dates and call back. Left on the recall list.

events.reason: Sudden severe shortness of breath and left chest pain after coughing

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Large left pneumothorax with collapse of the left lung. The mediastinum is shifted to the right. Right lung clear. No right-sided pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Large left pneumothorax with mediastinal shift.

reports.text: Portable AP chest after intervention. Left chest tube in place with its tip toward the apex. Left lung re-expanded. Mediastinum returned to midline. Endotracheal tube tip above the carina. Right lung clear.
reports.conclusion: Left lung re-expanded after chest tube placement; endotracheal tube in good position.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY MEDICAL CENTER, EMERGENCY SERVICES
Arrival 08/05/2026 16:42
Patient: Steven Sears, 49 M

HPI: 49-year-old man with COPD (GOLD Group C) and bronchiolitis obliterans diagnosed by his pulmonologist in February 2025, on fluticasone propionate/salmeterol since January 2025. Brought in after a violent bout of coughing at home, followed at once by severe breathlessness and pain in the left side of the chest. On arrival he is anxious and diaphoretic and can only get out a few words at a time.

Home meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily; fluticasone propionate/salmeterol 250/50 mcg twice daily; albuterol 90 mcg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: COPD; bronchiolitis obliterans. PSH: knee arthroscopy with meniscus repair, 2018.
Social: smokes 1.5 ppd, 45 pack-years. Former flavoring plant operator, on disability. Rare alcohol.
Family: father COPD; mother HTN and type 2 DM; brother asthma.

Triage vitals: BP 90/60, HR 122, RR 30, SpO2 88% on room air, T 37.2 C.

Exam: distended neck veins. Trachea displaced to the right. Left hemithorax hyperresonant with markedly decreased breath sounds; right side with air movement. Tachycardic, no murmur.

Portable CXR: large left pneumothorax with shift of the mediastinum.
ABG on room air: pH 7.32 / PaCO2 50 / PaO2 60 / HCO3 24.

ED course: clinical tension pneumothorax. Worsening rapidly. Needle decompression of the left chest at the second intercostal space, midclavicular line, with an audible rush of air and prompt improvement in blood pressure. Airway secured by rapid-sequence intubation for airway protection given his deterioration and fatigue. Left tube thoracostomy placed, connected to suction. Repeat film: left lung re-expanded, tube and ETT in good position. After decompression BP 112/70, HR 104, SpO2 95% on the ventilator.

Impression: left tension pneumothorax in a patient with COPD and bronchiolitis obliterans.
Disposition: admitted to the ICU, critical condition at time of transfer.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to let you know I was in the hospital last week. I had a bad coughing fit on the 5th and my left lung collapsed. They put a tube in my chest and a breathing tube down my throat and I was in the ICU. Breathing tube came out after 2 days, chest tube a few days after that, and I came home Wednesday the 12th. Same inhalers as before. They said no flying, quit smoking, and see my lung doctor and a chest surgeon about stopping it from happening again. I have some soreness where the tube was. Do you need to see me?

documents.title: Re: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Steven, I'm sorry you went through that, and glad you're home. Yes, I want to see you. The front desk will call Monday to book a visit, and we will request the hospital records. Please keep the pulmonology and surgery appointments. If you get sudden shortness of breath or chest pain again, call 911 right away, don't wait. Soreness at the tube site should ease over a couple of weeks; tell us if it gets red, swollen or drains.

documents.title: Hospital Records Request and Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested ED record and discharge summary from the hospital for the 08/05-08/12 stay. Called pt, booked post-hospital visit 09/03. Pt has a pulmonology visit later this month, surgery visit date not yet set.

documents.body: Received from the hospital: ED physician record, 08/05/2026 (4 pages). Discharge summary not included; hospital records office says it is not yet signed and will be faxed when finalized. Filed and routed to PCP.

documents.body: ED record reviewed: left tension pneumothorax 8/5, needle decompression, intubation, left chest tube, ICU. Awaiting discharge summary. Will go over everything at the 9/3 visit.
